document_title: 233 data centers never returned the water survey
_note: Slide strings read off the render report's text nodes and each frame's own source line by build_copy.py.
caption:
The water board asked by mail. Now ERCOT asks before the power flows.

Records the Texas Tribune obtained for 2020 through 2025 count 334 data center facilities. 233 never submitted a requested water use survey. The Tribune reports a fine of up to $500 for skipping it. The board says it has no authority of its own to prosecute.

Does ERCOT's request reach those 233? Its list is drawn differently. The survey goes only to operating data centers. The request reaches proposed ones of 25 to under 75 MW classed as Substantiated and Batch Zero facilities or additions not yet energized.

ERCOT's September 14th notice puts the water board's questions in Section C. A complete response carries a notarized attestation. A failure to respond is reported to the PUC and the Office of the Governor.

Will the report ERCOT expects to publish by December 10th say how many responded?

#ERCOT #TWDB #BatchZero

S1.headline: Asked how much water they use, 233 never answered.
S1.body: Records the Texas Tribune obtained for 2020 through 2025 count 334 data center facilities. Of those, 101 returned the water board's survey at least once. One bore for each facility, drawn to illustrate.
strings: Asked how much water they use, 233 never answered.

Records the Texas Tribune obtained for 2020 through 2025 count 334 data center facilities. Of those, 101 returned the water board's survey at least once. One bore for each facility, drawn to illustrate.

S2.headline: 101 answered, 233 never did
S2.body: A brass plug seals the bore of each facility that returned a survey at least once. No bore stands for a named facility. The plate is drawn to illustrate.
strings: A brass plug seals the bore of each facility that returned a survey at least once. No bore stands for a named facility. The plate is drawn to illustrate.

S3.headline: Up to $500
S3.body: Skipping the survey is a Class C misdemeanor, the Tribune reports. The water board says it has no authority of its own to prosecute. State officials don't know whether any misdemeanor penalty has been issued against a data center.
strings: Skipping the survey is a Class C misdemeanor, the Tribune reports. The water board says it has no authority of its own to prosecute. State officials don't know whether any misdemeanor penalty has been issued against a data center.

S4.headline: The survey's line is 10 million gallons a year
S4.body: It goes to operating facilities using more than that, the Tribune reports. This tank holds that much, drawn to illustrate. The survey doesn't ask how a data center cools its servers.
strings: The survey's line is 10 million gallons a year

S5.headline: 97 facilities reported 1.4 billion gallons
S5.body: The Tribune reports the total from last year's survey. That much would fill 140 tanks of 10 million gallons, drawn here to illustrate.
strings: The Tribune reports the total from last year's survey. That much would fill 140 tanks of 10 million gallons, drawn here to illustrate.

S6.headline: Now the grid operator asks
S6.body: ERCOT's September 14th notice carries the water board's questions in Section C, developed with the PUC and the board. ERCOT forwards the answers to the board. The transformer is drawn to illustrate.
strings: ERCOT's September 14th notice carries the water board's questions in Section C, developed with the PUC and the board. ERCOT forwards the answers to the board. The transformer is drawn to illustrate.

S7.headline: The request reaches what isn't energized yet
S7.cite: c3 c4 c5 c6 c7 c40
S7.body: It goes to proposed data centers of 25 to under 75 MW whose load is classified as Substantiated. It also goes to Batch Zero facilities or additions not yet energized at 60 kV or above. The survey goes to operating data centers.

S8.headline: A notarized answer was due October 12th
S8.body: The developer's own utility files each response. A complete one carries a notarized attestation. A failure to respond is reported to the PUC and the Office of the Governor.
strings: A notarized answer was due October 12th

S9.headline: ERCOT expects a report by December 10th
S9.body: ERCOT says the report will set out conclusions from its own review, with the PUC. A case over a skipped survey is up to local officials, the Tribune reports. A bigger fine needs the Legislature, which meets in Austin in January.
